decisions.reason: Although no longer visibly marketed, the chart visualization plugin draws directly on the firm's web-GIS platform knowledge and is more likely to be retained or folded into the core suite than discontinued outright.

The hierarchical search plugin remains close to the firm's established geospatial search and integration capabilities, so its knowledge fit supports continued use even if it is no longer promoted as a standalone item.

This mobile layer-control component is technically related to the firm's UX and mobile GIS work, but its narrow scope and lack of recent visibility make consolidation somewhat more likely than for the core platform.
As the firm's flagship GIS solution platform and a central vehicle for applying its accumulated R&D, standards, and integration capabilities, it is very unlikely to be taken off the market.

Mobile field data capture is a strong adjacent application for an enterprise geospatial specialist with in-house R&D, so it is still more likely to be developed and integrated into projects than withdrawn.

The search extension for web map apps fits the firm's installed technical base and customer needs well, and the most plausible path is continued commercialization or integration rather than market exit.
